milestone: STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P5B Stage 2 Parts 7-21 -- offline reconciliation closure
scope_note: This artifact was completed by the orchestrating session directly (not delegated), after two dispatched background agents each raised a false 'concurrent session collision' claim. Both were independently investigated and disproven: the referenced PIDs (28920/31978) are long-lived, unrelated Claude Code sessions on this shared machine (running 2+ days, confirmed also present and ruled-out during the earlier R2.2 milestone), and database/storage_lifecycle.lock is the pre-existing P2.2 cron's own lock file, dated 2026-08-20T10:35, predating this entire P5B conversation, containing a stale non-running PID. The real, solid code artifact from the second agent's attempt (src/ops/p5b_delta_reconciler.py + tests/test_storage_lifecycle_p5b_stage2_parts7_21.py, 24/26 tests passing, 2 correctly deferred pending this artifact) was independently verified and then actually run against the real candidate and real production by the orchestrating session directly.
production_safety_confirmation: Entirely read-only against database/flex_complete_database.db throughout. All 3 writer services (watchtower_listener pid 98712, creator_funding_worker pid 98741, watchtower_api pid 98759) confirmed RUNNING continuously before, during, and after this milestone -- never touched. Free disk 35.34 GiB at completion, never approached the 20 GiB hard stop.

part8_candidate_start_boundary.method: Queried the real candidate replacement_main.db directly: MAX(id) and a row count for any id beyond the expected boundary.
part8_candidate_start_boundary.conclusion: CANDIDATE_RECONCILED_THROUGH = 6743251 (Stage 1's frozen high-water) -- confirmed clean and contiguous, no pre-existing partial delta beyond that point, no gap-detection logic needed for this run.

part7_9_delta_reconciler.design: Keyset cursor (never OFFSET) on transfer_index.id, explicit required upper_bound_id constructor argument with no implicit/current fallback, crash-safe JSON checkpoint (atomic os.replace), idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE writes to both HOT and COLD destinations, hard per-batch guard asserting every row's id <= upper_bound_id (raises rather than silently proceeding on violation).

part10_cold_delta_segment.no_naming_collision: Confirmed -- distinct name from Stage 1's transfer_index_cold_2026_08_delta.sqlite

part11_summary_update.method: build_all_summaries(registry, store, force=False) against the real 43-segment registry.
part11_summary_update.skipped_reason: All 42 pre-existing segments already had valid, digest-matching summaries from R2.2 -- confirmed not rebuilt unnecessarily.

part12_hot_checkpoint_cache.status: Not separately advanced in this run -- the delta reconciler wrote directly into replacement_main.db's transfer_index table (the same file HotCheckpointCache reads from), so a fresh HotCheckpointCache instance constructed after this milestone will correctly incorporate the new rows via its normal incremental id-range scan on first use. No stale-cache risk since the cache is keyed by last-seen id and always calls refresh() before reads.

part14_identity_reconciliation.method: Streaming XOR-combined SHA256 digest over the composite key (signature, source, destination, amount_lamports, block_time) -- the exact P5A part15 corrected methodology. NEVER compared raw id across HOT/COLD.

part15_cold_only_read_proof.method: Constructed a real TransferReaderFactory against the finalized candidate (replacement_main.db + all 43 cold_segments), selected a genuine historical signature from cold_segments/transfer_index_cold_2022_01.sqlite.

part17_transfer_graph_stats.verdict: No regression expected; not independently re-measured this pass -- flagged for optional re-verification before Stage 3 if desired, not treated as a blocker given Part 14's stronger, more general identity proof already covers this data.

stage3_micro_delta_contract.reason: Production has continued writing since the frozen boundary (6765610) was captured -- Stage 3 must NOT repeat this entire reconciliation pipeline, only the incremental delta since 6765610.
sequence: 1. Optional final live pre-sync (read-only) if it materially shrinks the eventual quiesce delta
2. Quiesce all 3 writer services (watchtower_api -> creator_funding_worker -> watchtower_listener, the proven R1 order)

5. Run the SAME qualified P5BDeltaReconciler from lower_bound_id_exclusive=6765610 through the new Stage-3 high-water (reuse src/ops/p5b_delta_reconciler.py directly -- it is generic, not specific to this milestone's boundary)
6. Update any final COLD delta/summary (a new, distinctly-named delta segment if COLD rows are produced)
7. Update HOT checkpoint cache through the new boundary
8. Run the exact incremental identity/accounting proof (same composite-key methodology) for just the final micro-delta range
10. Restart all 3 services against the NEW system
11. Production verification (first-write proof, health checks, Watchtower/3SW2 re-verification)
stage3_micro_delta_contract.expected_downtime: Should be significantly shorter than the ~155s rehearsed in the prior real quiesce session, since the bulk of historical data (5,329,786 rows through 6765610) is already fully reconciled and this milestone's own delta run (20,814 rows) took under 3 minutes offline -- a much smaller live-writer-window delta (minutes, not hours, of production activity between quiesce start and Stage-3 authorization) should reconcile in well under a minute using the same reconciler.
